stem.en: Pancreatic cells secrete large amounts of protein. Which parts would you expect to be well developed in these cells?

text.en: Chloroplasts and a thick cell wall, which are needed before any protein can be made.

feedback.en: Pancreatic cells are animal cells, so they have neither of these.

text.en: Smooth ER and large central vacuoles, because proteins are stored in the vacuoles before use.

feedback.en: Smooth ER is involved with fats and hormones, and animal cells have no large central vacuole.

text.en: The nucleolus only, because it builds every protein that will leave the cell in one piece.

feedback.en: The nucleolus makes ribosomal subunits, not secreted proteins.

explanation.en: Rough ER carries ribosomes and is mainly involved in protein synthesis and secretion, and the Golgi apparatus packages the proteins into vesicles.
